*Turn a Bible verse or chapter into a researched, one-page Bible study for a group.*

> **Every historical or interpretive claim must be grounded in the Bible or an identified Christian source; never invent certainty where Christian sources disagree.**

## Why install this

A verse can be familiar while its setting is not. This skill researches the passage before
condensing it into one page your group can read, discuss, and keep. Dates stay qualified,
related verses come with explanations, and every research section links to its evidence.

## What you get

| Artifact | Purpose |
|---|---|
| PDF and PNG | One-page handout for printing or sharing |
| HTML | Responsive study with linked sources |
| Research JSON | Claim citations and source review notes |

- Writing date and authorship, separated from the time of the narrated events.
- Historical and literary context, meaning, and three related passages.
- A 45-minute participant guide: six observation/interpretation questions, three
  cross-reference exercises, writing space, a weekly commitment, and prayer.
- One-page PDF, high-resolution PNG, responsive HTML, and a research JSON record.
- A Christian-only research policy, with explicit acknowledgment of interpretive differences.

## Quick start

From this repository checkout, install the local plugin in Codex:

```bash
codex plugin marketplace add "$PWD"
codex plugin add bible-study@claude-skills
```

Start a new session and invoke `$bible-study John 3`. In Claude Code, after this version
is available from the marketplace:

```text
$bible-study
```

```text
/plugin marketplace add natejswenson/claude-skills
/plugin install bible-study@claude-skills
/bible-study John 3
```

The skill researches the passage using your host's web tools. To reproduce the reviewed
John 3 handout offline, run from `skills/bible-study/skills/bible-study`:

```bash
node scripts/bible-study.js validate --file evals/input/john-3.json
node scripts/bible-study.js render --file evals/input/john-3.json --out /tmp/john-3
python3 scripts/export.py --file /tmp/john-3/study.html --out /tmp/john-3
```

## Triggers

“Create a Bible study”, “study John 3”, or “make a Bible study handout”. Supports individual
verses, passages and whole chapters; honors a requested translation or Christian tradition.
Defaults: adult small group and public-domain World English Bible quotations.

## Requirements

- **Claude Code:** Use the host's web, file, and shell tools; no Claude CLI subprocess is needed.
- **Codex:** Use Codex's web, file, and shell tools with the same bundled renderer.
- **Personal data:** No credentials or private configuration store. Outputs go to your chosen folder.

See [Codex migration notes](https://github.com/natejswenson/claude-skills/blob/main/docs/codex-migration.md) for shared-host conventions.

Node 18+ for offline validation and HTML. Python 3 with Playwright and Chromium for PDF/PNG:

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/python -m pip install playwright
.venv/bin/python -m playwright install chromium
```

Use `.venv/bin/python` for export when using that environment. Poppler (`pdfinfo`,
`pdftoppm`) verifies page count and renders the PDF for inspection. No API credentials
or Claude CLI required. Both hosts use the same implementation and their own web tools.

## Evidence and limits

Research uses Scripture and identified Christian sources only. Software checks source
attestations and citation structure; it cannot determine whether a publisher is Christian
or a theological claim is sound. The agent must read and assess the evidence. The John 3
example was researched on September 19, 2026 using Scripture and four Christian publishers.

The renderer escapes content and refuses incomplete bundles. Export blocks remote resources
and rejects overflowing pages; visual inspection remains a delivery requirement. Files are
created locally; distributing them to your group is a separate action you control.

## Development

Run `npm test` in the nested skill directory. The baseline re-renders the reviewed John 3
research offline and checks the HTML, with a negative source-policy case. It does not
pretend to test live research or a model's theology. Other tests reject absent evidence,
missing uncertainty, invalid URLs, and excessive content, and check HTML escaping.

After a newly reviewed real run, refresh with:

```bash
node scripts/refresh-baseline.mjs --from /absolute/path/to/reviewed-run
```

Source-declared CI and release wiring are included. Live branch protection must be applied
by an administrator after the reviewed change lands; no release is cut automatically.
